source.title: Neural Networks for Bayesian Inverse Problems Governed by a Nonlinear ODE
source.authors: Germán Villalobos; J. Rudi; Andreas Mang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports prediction error across neural-network sizes and training-sample sizes, but does not reproduce the original double-descent setup or measure interpolation thresholds.
record.gate_note: The architecture and sample-size sweeps report prediction accuracy on validation or testing data and are retained. The paper does not report an epoch-wise test-error curve, locate an interpolation threshold, or test whether any peak is predicted by effective complexity. Its brief bias–variance discussion cites prior work but is not itself a result.
record.test_reason: This methods paper trains DNN/CNN estimators for FitzHugh–Nagumo parameter inference. Double descent appears only as a passing citation of Belkin et al. in Remark 2.2. The size sweep (Tables 11–12) and sample sweeps (Tables 17–18) report the method's own test or validation accuracy. They report no training error, no interpolation threshold and no fit regime, so they cannot show a double-descent peak. The sweeps are also coarse: 6–7 sizes and 5 sample counts. Neither sweep was designed to bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that NN estimators jointly recover ODE parameters, noise parameters and posterior covariances with single-digit relative errors. They add that TS&FC features are needed, that at least about 2,000 training samples are required, and that dedicated hardware cuts training time 8–14x. Scaling network size reaches a 'pivotal point' in accuracy. They draw no conclusion about double descent; Remark 2.2 only cites prior work that modern networks can escape the bias–variance trade-off.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates supervised inverse-problem estimators and reports prediction accuracy across architecture and data-size sweeps; it does not use the original double-descent experimental setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction performance varies with architecture and feature choice; the paper reports that using time-series plus Fourier features performs best for several estimation tasks. Sample-size results also depend on whether training data include noise.
record.problems: The size sweep does not report training fit or locate interpolation thresholds. Results for the architecture sweep use a single stated testing setup, and the relevant test-MSE tables give no uncertainty estimates. Sample-size sweeps use validation data and do not target the interpolation regime.
record.rows_left_out: Architecture-exploration results in Tables 4–5 and supplementary Tables 15–16 report validation accuracy for many layer/filter combinations, but are omitted because the tables do not state trainable-parameter counts for each cell and the Section 3.5 testing tables provide the clearer size sweeps. Other sample-size sweeps in Tables 6–8 and 19 are omitted to stay within 60 rows; the retained Tables 17–18 give sample-size results for model-parameter prediction under the three stated noise configurations.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests' and T2 labels are not justified. The only link to the phenomenon is a citation (Belkin et al. 2019, an original source) in Remark 2.2. The size and sample sweeps are coarse evaluations of the study's own method: no training error, no interpolation threshold, and dropout on the DNNs. The noted small rises at the largest sizes are single points with no later descent. All rows are reassigned to 'none' and no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies DNN and CNN sizes and reports testing error, but does not report training error or identify the size that just fits the training set.
No test-error curve over training epochs is reported.
Training-sample sizes are varied and validation error is reported, but the study does not locate or specifically test a neighborhood of an interpolation threshold.
No comparison across general model classes or test of a general double-descent curve is reported.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested across size, epochs, and sample count.
Noise is varied in prediction experiments, but the study does not test its effect on a double-descent peak, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not compare parameter counts with an effective number of parameters or test whether that changes the curve shape.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CNN and DNN size sweeps in Section 3.5
reader_labels.reason: Testing MSE generally improves over the listed sizes, then rises slightly at the largest listed size; the study does not locate the just-fit threshold or show a subsequent descent (rows V1-CNN-2 through V1-CNN-128 and V1-DNN-128 through V1-DNN-4096).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Training-sample sweeps in Supplementary material, Tables 17–18
reader_labels.reason: Validation MdAPE often declines as training size increases, while the noise-free-training/noisy-validation settings can worsen at larger sizes; none of these sweeps identifies an interpolation threshold, so they do not establish the claimed near-threshold effect (rows V3-DNN-00-500 through V3-CNN-11-8000).
